Overview

Purpose: This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference sales-facing assets: positioning and messaging, competitor brief, pitch-deck guidance, pricing negotiation guidance, customer case studies, and a security FAQ tailored for prospects. Use this doc as the canonical reference for AEs, solution engineers, and sales ops during opportunity pursuit.

Audience: Account Executives, Solutions Engineers, Sales Leadership, Sales Enablement, and Customer Success.

Contents (quick nav):
- Core positioning & elevator pitch
- Competitive brief (top competitors and battle-card)
- Recommended pitch deck structure and demo checklist
- Pricing guidance & negotiation playbook
- Case studies (two customer examples with metrics)
- Security FAQ for prospects (common questions + approved answers)
- Sales assets and next steps

### 1. Core positioning & messaging

Short elevator pitch (15-30s):
Redwood Inference is a developer-first production inference platform that delivers predictable, low-latency LLM serving with unified controls across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments, so engineering teams get enterprise-grade reliability and cost-efficiency without building their own serving stack.

Top 3 value propositions (customer-facing bullets):
- Production economics: Reduce per-token costs with intelligent batching, KV/prefix caching, and model quantization profiles while maintaining production latency SLOs.
- Unified deployment: One API, consistent rollout controls, and the same operational tooling whether you run hosted, reserved (Dedicated), or private (VPC/on-prem).
- Reliability & compliance: SLA-backed Dedicated tiers, private deployment options with KMS/HSM support, and audit logs for regulated workloads.

Target personas and messaging hooks:
- ML/Inference Engineers: "Focus on model quality; we handle high-throughput inference, caching, and kernel optimizations."
- Platform Engineers: "Standardize inference across teams with predictable latency and autoscaling policies."
- Product Engineering / PMs: "Ship LLM features with consistent user experience across regions and capacity tiers."

Objection handling (short scripts):
1) "Your pricing is higher than self-hosting"  - Response: "Self-hosting shifts engineering and ops cost into your stack. Redwood reduces TCO by optimizing utilization (batching/caching), providing hardened ops, and accelerating time-to-market. For Dedicated customers we provide ROI modeling vs build/buy during scoping."
2) "We need air-gapped on-prem"  - Response: "We offer Private/on-prem packaging with a customer-controlled control plane and optional air-gapped deployment; we also integrate with KMS/HSM for key control."

### 2. Competitive brief (battle-card)

Competitors covered: OpenAI (hosted API), Anthropic, Major cloud provider managed endpoints (AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex), and self-hosting (customers building their own stack).

Quick matrix (summary):
| Dimension | Redwood | OpenAI / Anthropic | Cloud managed endpoints | Self-hosting |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Deployment flexibility | Hosted / Dedicated / Private | Hosted only | Hosted (cloud-specific) | Fully flexible but high ops |
| Cost controls | Batching, caching, quantization suggestions, reserved capacity | Limited to model choice and quota | Varies; often higher for inference | Depends on infra efficiency |
| Enterprise features (SLA, audit logs) | SLA-backed Dedicated, audit logs, KMS | Enterprise agreements available, but limited private deployment | Enterprise controls tied to cloud | Depends on engineering |
| Performance tuning | Kernel selection, runtime optimizations | Model-optimized backend | Varies | Full control but high effort |

Top sales plays vs each competitor:
- Against OpenAI/Anthropic: Lead with predictable latency and cost controls for high-volume production workloads. Emphasize Dedicated and caching to drive down per-token costs at scale.
- Against cloud endpoints: Position Redwood as vendor-agnostic with portability and the ability to run private deployments outside a single cloud provider.
- Against self-hosting: Emphasize time-to-value, operational maturity, and measurable unit economics (provide an ROI worksheet).

Battle-card quick bullets for reps (keep on single slide):
- Win themes: predictability, unified runtime, cost efficiency, enterprise controls.
- Lose themes: early-stage prototypes where cost is negligible and simplicity matters (point them to Hosted API as low-friction option).
- Demo hooks: tracing per-request latency, model rollouts/canary, and cost-per-1000-token dashboard.

### 3. Pitch deck & demo structure

Recommended slide order (10-12 slides):
1) Cover + customer logo
2) Problem statement & business impact (latency, cost, reliability risks)
3) Vision & Redwood value prop
4) Product overview (Hosted, Dedicated, Private)
5) How it works at a high level (serving runtime, caching, smart routing)
6) Performance & cost benchmarks (include internal perf numbers)
7) Security & compliance (SOC2, KMS, private deployments)
8) Case study (results + metrics)
9) Pricing options & deployment roadmap
10) Rollout plan + success milestones
11) Contracting & support options (SLA tiers, onboarding)
12) Call to action

Demo checklist (for SEs):
1) Warm up the environment and confirm model versions.
2) Show a live generation call; enable streaming to highlight latency.
3) Open Console dashboard: show per-route cost, token breakdown, and latency SLO charts.
4) Demonstrate a canary rollout (deploy new model variant and trigger fallback).
5) Show role-based access and audit log sample.
6) If security-sensitive buyer, demo Private deployment architecture (reference diagram).

Standard demo script (3-5 mins per section):
- 0:00-2:00 Product overview + key differentiators
- 2:00-6:00 Live generation + latency/cost dashboard
- 6:00-9:00 Rollout & security features
- 9:00-12:00 Q&A / next steps

### 4. Pricing guidance & negotiation playbook

Pricing models (short):
- Hosted API (usage-based): per-token pricing tiers for generations and embeddings; volume discounts kick in at 10M tokens/month and above.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly/annual commit for GPU pools, billed on reserved vGPU units + usage for burst.
- Private (enterprise): platform license + deployment and support fees; optional professional services for on-prem setup.

Example pricing guidance (do not quote without Legal approval - use as negotiation framework):
- Hosted: $0.0008 / input token, $0.002 / output token (example anchor). Volume tiers: 0-10M, 10-100M (10% discount), 100M+ (20%+).
- Dedicated: baseline reserve $60k/month for a 4-card A100-equivalent pool with 99.9% uptime SLA; additional throughput billed at $X per vGPU-hour.
- Private: one-time platform license $150k-$500k depending on scope, plus annual support 18-25% of license.

Negotiation playbook (steps):
1) Discovery: document expected tokens/day, peak qps, latency targets, data residency/security requirements.
2) Build ROI: use internal ROI worksheet to model per-token cost vs self-hosting and competitor quotes.
3) Propose initial offer: anchor with Hosted API for POC or Dedicated reserve for production.
4) Concessions guideline: discount bands tied to multi-year commit, increase in spend, or referrals. Always get legal approval for >25% discount.
5) Closing: propose pilot acceptance criteria and success metrics (latency SLOs, throughput, cost per 1k tokens).

Pricing approvals: any non-standard pricing or contract language must be approved by Sales Ops and Legal.

### 5. Case studies (sales-ready summaries)

Case study: Acme Health (anonymized) - HealthTech customer
- Challenge: Real-time clinical note summarization at scale with strict PHI requirements and on-prem data residency.
- Solution: Private deployment with on-prem inference nodes, KMS integration, and inference caching for common prefixes.
- Outcome: 45% reduction in per-note cost vs prior cloud endpoint, 60% faster tail latency (p95), and successful SOC2 Type II audit support during their compliance review.
- Key metrics to call out: 45% cost reduction, p95 latency improved from 900ms -> 360ms, full deployment in 8 weeks.

Case study: FinTech Co. (anonymized) - Consumer finance application
- Challenge: High-throughput conversational assistant with strict latency and cost targets during peak account opening flows.
- Solution: Dedicated reserved capacity with canary rollouts and automatic fallback to smaller model variants on burst.
- Outcome: 30% lower average cost per session vs previous managed endpoint; rollout reduced incident rate by 70% during model updates.
- Key metrics: 30% cost savings, incident rate down 70%, successful phased rollout to 200k users over 6 months.

Assets to attach to customer-facing deck: full case study PDFs, anonymized benchmark CSVs, ROI worksheet, short video testimonial (when available).

### 6. Security FAQ for prospects (approved responses)

Q: Where is my data stored and processed?
A: Redwood supports regional data residency. Hosted API defaults to the customer-selected region; Dedicated and Private deployments keep inference and telemetry in customer-controlled networks. For Private/on-prem, data never leaves your network unless explicitly configured.

Q: Do you support encryption at rest and in transit?
A: Yes. All data in transit uses TLS 1.2+; at-rest encryption is supported via provider-managed keys or customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM).

Q: Can we bring our own keys (BYOK)?
A: Yes. We support BYOK via integrations with AWS KMS, Google KMS, and HSM providers for Private and Dedicated deployments. Hosted API customers can enable customer-managed keys on eligible plans.

Q: What compliance certifications do you have?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and is in process for ISO 27001. We provide compliance evidence packages for enterprise customers under an NDA.

Q: How do you handle logging and audit trails?
A: We store structured audit logs with per-request metadata including model version, route, and requesting token. Logs can be forwarded to customer SIEMs (Splunk, Datadog) or exported for retention in customer storage for Dedicated/Private customers.

Q: What is your incident response and notification policy?
A: We maintain an incident response process with an SLA for notifications to customers on severity-1 incidents. Dedicated customers receive a dedicated oncall contact and post-incident review with root cause analysis.

Q: How do you protect against model leakage and data exfiltration?
A: Multiple controls: model sandboxing, rate limits, per-token output filters, and optional request/response scrubbing. For sensitive workloads we recommend Private deployments and redaction policies implemented at the application layer.

Q: Can we audit your code or run a penetration test?
A: We perform regular third-party pen tests and internal code reviews. Enterprise customers may request pen-test arrangements for Private/on-prem deployments under a written agreement.

Q: What SLAs do you offer?
A: Hosted API provides best-effort availability. Dedicated customers are eligible for SLA-backed uptime guarantees (e.g., 99.9%) and latency SLOs defined in the contract. See the SLA template attached to the RFP response pack.

5) Submit draft to Sales Ops for final review.
